items.title: Who is Narrating the Future? AI and the Audiobook Market
items.excerpt: A Frankfurter Buchmesse white paper produced by Dosdoce.com surveys 85 audio industry experts: 85% now use AI somewhere in audiobook production, but only 17% have embedded it across more than six phases.

items.title: How AI wiped out an entire industry in Nairobi
items.excerpt: At its peak at least 40,000 people in Nairobi wrote academic papers for foreign students; after ChatGPT launched in 2022 prices and orders collapsed, leaving 'humanizers' who rework AI text.

items.title: "A Secure Environment to Explore": the AI Sandbox Initiative For Staff at the Library of Congress
items.excerpt: The Library of Congress's AI Sandbox for staff supported over a dozen small-scale experiments on real collections, from talking books to non-Latin manuscripts.

items.title: AI Use in The Scholarly Kitchen
items.excerpt: TSK restates its AI policy after daily reader accusations: AI cannot be credited as author, AI images are barred, but disclosed AI drafting/editing is allowed — and detectors can't tell generated from enhanced.

items.title: Opinion: You Have More Agency Than You Think: Creative Writing and Publishing in the Age of AI
items.excerpt: Indie author Nigel George argues AI externalizes cognition rather than replacing it, and that writers keep agency by drawing an explicit line about where AI may not touch the page.

items.title: Digital Books: HathiTrust Awarded $5 Million, 5-Year Mellon Grant to Enable AI-Driven Access and Discovery
items.excerpt: HathiTrust receives a five-year Mellon grant to open new AI-driven paths into its digitized book collections for researchers, students and the public.

items.title: Production Companies, Literary Agents, Foreign Languages: AI-Driven Scams Continue to Morph
items.excerpt: AI-driven author scams have expanded from marketing offers into impersonation of agents, editors, festivals and production companies — while the underlying markers stay unchanged.

items.title: News Summary: Google Play Books Launches Expert Intelligence Ebook Function
items.excerpt: Google Play Books adds Expert Intelligence, letting readers question purchased nonfiction ebooks using only the licensed text.

items.title: Guest Post — From Charity to Intellectual Partnership: The Global Monograph Crisis, AI, and the Future of Open Access Through the Lens of Ukraine
items.excerpt: Ukraine's academic publishing sector confronts the global monograph crisis with AI and open access.

items.title: New Directions Seminar: What Is a Journal in 2030?
items.excerpt: An SSP seminar asks what a journal becomes when AI mediates discovery and reading.

items.title: Authors Guild publishes survey results about copyright registration failures
items.excerpt: An Authors Guild survey finds many publishers never registered copyrights, a gap exposed by the Anthropic settlement claims process.

items.title: News Summary: Survey Suggests Many Publishers Still Fail to Register Copyright
items.excerpt: A postscript to the Anthropic case: an Authors Guild survey shows widespread failure to register copyright.

items.title: Around the Book World: Monday, September 7th, 2026
items.excerpt: Weekly roundup of international book-industry news including AI items.

items.title: E-Books: Google Announces Launch of "Expert Intelligence" Feature For Gemini Notebook
items.excerpt: Google introduces Expert Intelligence, a cross-Google initiative surfacing licensed book content inside Gemini's notebook.
